ns2:group.ns2:description:
Bradford and Bryan Manning have spent their lives adapting to a world built for sight. Both brothers live with Stargardt disease, which has taken much of their central vision and made everyday tasks like navigating a crowded street far more difficult.
Today, they use ChatGPT to turn visual information into something they can hear, understand, and act on. It helps them navigate unfamiliar places, analyze data, keep up with email, and run Two Blind Brothers, the nonprofit they founded to support the blind community.
Follow Bradford and Bryan as they move through New York, build their business, and use ChatGPT to create more independence in their own lives while expanding what feels possible for the community they serve.

ns2:group.ns2:title: Discovering new antibiotics with ChatGPT
ns2:group.ns2:description:
The de la Fuente Lab is using ChatGPT and Codex in the search for new molecules that could help fight antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
Modern medicine relies on effective antibiotics, which help us recover from routine illnesses, surgeries, childbirth, and more. However, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing problem. Approximately 5 million people die every year from bacterial AMR, and that number is expected to double by 2050. Dr. César de la Fuente and his team use ChatGPT and Codex to explore the genetic code of living and extinct organisms like woolly mammoths, snake venom, and more to identify promising antibiotic molecules. Work that traditionally takes five or six years can now be done in a matter of hours.

ns2:group.ns2:title: XConf India 2026 - wrap up
ns2:group.ns2:description: In 2026, XConf India returned to Hyderabad, bringing together 580 technologists, 31 speakers and 15 expert sessions for a day of hands-on workshops, technical talks and interactive demos across AI-first software delivery, agentic AI systems and the risks of emerging AI technologies. ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]The AI Kill Chain | Track3-03 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: The AI Kill Chain | Track3-03 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
AI vulnerabilities rarely cause major incidents alone. Impact emerges when weaknesses chain across AI systems, identities, tools, data, and business processes.
This talk introduces the AI Kill Chain through realistic scenarios and a live demo, showing how prompt injection enables tool abuse, poisoned knowledge influences decisions, agent memory creates persistence, and agent trust enables lateral movement. See how least-privilege agents, tool authorization, trust boundaries, human approval, and secure architecture can break the chain.
Leave with a practical methodology to identify, model, and mitigate AI attack chains before they become breaches.
Demo link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1l53XbHOIM3vhYkwnXsuEc_oDVy8hJAM-/view?usp=sharing

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]One guardrail is not enough: Defense-in-depth against LLM jailbreaks | Track3-02 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: One guardrail is not enough: Defense-in-depth against LLM jailbreaks | Track3-02 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Production chatbots have been talked into binding contracts, creating legal liability, and leaking data through RAG. OWASP ranks prompt injection as the #1 GenAI risk and notes that RAG and fine-tuning do not eliminate it.
This talk presents a defense-in-depth architecture on AWS, reframing jailbreaks as two problems: a universal safety baseline inherited from the model and a bot-specific scope envelope that teams must define. Explore the pipeline: a fine-tuned BERT classifier on SageMaker, moderation and PII filtering, an LLM canonicalizer, hostile-input retrieval, guarded generation, and output filtering. Close the loop with asynchronous LLM-as-judge triage that turns production attacks into training data, continuously strengthening the cheapest defense layer. Demo link :- https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hoaXYTaz6o5WNGe-fyQ3Fz7bGOsu3E3F/view?usp=drive_link

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Human in the loop is not enough | Track3-01 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: Human in the loop is not enough | Track3-01 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
"Shipping an AI product is easy; securing it is where teams get caught off guard. We share lessons from building an enterprise AI platform on a third-party foundation model, where human oversight proved insufficient as the platform evolved toward autonomous and agentic capabilities.
Explore practical security lessons across governance, risk, cloud architecture, threat modelling, penetration testing, and guardrails for systems that act, not just respond. See how risks evolved from OWASP Top 10 for web apps to LLM and Agentic Apps."

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]TFM based Shared Intelligence Layer | Track2-03 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: TFM based Shared Intelligence Layer | Track2-03 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Augmenting your existing AI/ML models Every model in a bank sits on its own feature pipeline, compressing the same customer event stream into aggregates that discard ordering and timing. Transaction Foundation Models learn from the sequence instead. This session explores what a shared intelligence layer changes for models already in production, what augmenting existing models involves, and how the NVIDIA stack and blueprint make the build methodical and repeatable. Includes a live demonstration.
Demo link: https://tfmgnndecksite.vercel.app"

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Deep research at scale | Track2-02 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: Deep research at scale | Track2-02 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Deep research at scale - Evolving from LangGraph to DeepAgents across 15M+ documents Scaling LLMs to 15M+ domain-heavy documents exposes the limits of standard RAG. Complex enterprise queries demand multi-hop reasoning, multi-document synthesis, and strict domain accuracy.
We share our blueprint for taking a multi-agent deep research engine from prototype to production, covering HPC-based retrieval, the evolution from LangGraph ReAct to DeepAgents, and evaluation using reranking, LLM-as-a-judge, custom rubrics, and human verification. We also share lessons from MLflow observability, streaming logs, and Bedrock infrastructure.
Learn what it takes to reliably bring non-deterministic agentic workflows into production at scale."

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]But it worked in my PoC! | Track2-01 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: But it worked in my PoC! | Track2-01 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
"What does it take to automate enterprise IT at scale with AI agents? More than expected. This talk shares the hard-won lessons from deploying agents to manage software updates across thousands of devices globally. Our first attempt collapsed under bloated prompts. The second relied on an all-knowing orchestrator that consumed 80% of its context, took two minutes to respond, burned 3M tokens per run, and hallucinated its way to failure. The third shipped.
Discover what finally worked: smaller agents with tighter responsibilities, on-demand skills, structured agent-to-agent communication, dynamic agent spawning, deterministic workflows, dedicated Q&A, and tool-call validation. Learn why multi-agent systems are a distributed systems problem first and an AI problem second. No theory. Pure scar tissue."

ns2:group.ns2:title: Engineering the harness | Track1-02 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description: Your AI coding agent isn't the problem, the harness around it is. In "Engineering the Harness," we explore why smart models ignore team conventions, then share a practical system of guides that steer agents before they act and sensors that catch mistakes after. Drawing from a brownfield multi-repo platform and a greenfield agentic workflow, we show how to build a setup that works with any AI tool or stack. ns2:group.ns2:title: AI First Legacy Migration | Track1-01 | Xconf India 2026

Stateful test-driven generation, automated validation, and iterative self-correction ensure behavioural equivalence while reducing migration effort and risk. The process also surfaces undocumented business logic and edge cases, giving teams deeper insight into legacy systems.

ns2:group.ns2:title: iPhone Duo Hands-On: I’m VERY Impressed
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone is finally here. I went hands-on with the brand new iPhone Duo, and after spending some time with Apple’s $1,999 foldable, I’m impressed.
The iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch folding inner display, 5.4-inch outer display, titanium design, A20 Pro chip, dual 48-megapixel cameras, MagSafe, and an incredibly thin design. Apple has also put a huge amount of work into minimizing the display crease with a new nanotexture finish and redesigned folding display.
But some of the most interesting parts of the iPhone Duo are the software. iOS adapts to the larger folding display, supports two apps side-by-side, introduces new half-folded experiences, and even turns the Duo into a standalone StandBy display without needing to be connected to a charger.
There are still some questions, including the lack of a telephoto camera, limited multitasking controls, long-term hinge durability, and of course that $1,999 starting price.
These are my first impressions after going hands-on with the iPhone Duo. A full review is coming soon, so let me know what you want me to test!

ns2:group.ns2:title: New AirPods 5: Everything announced about the best Active Noise Cancellation in an open-ear design
ns2:group.ns2:description:
AirPods 5 deliver up to 1.5x more Active Noise Cancellation than the previous generation, with a redesigned acoustic architecture for richer, more detailed sound. Transparency lets you hear the world around you. Personalized Spatial Audio places sound all around you. Live Translation helps you communicate across languages. And you get hands-free access to the new Siri AI, an even more powerful and personalized AI assistant on your iPhone. Available in two models. Listen for hours with AirPods 5. And AirPods 5 with Wireless Charging Case add up to an extra hour of battery life on a single charge.
Best Active Noise Cancellation in an open-ear design evaluation tested in July 2026 in accordance with IEC 60268-24 as compared with best-selling commercially available wireless open-ear headphones without ear tips.
Up to 1.5x more Active Noise Cancellation compared with AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation when tested in accordance with IEC 60268-24.
Personalized Spatial Audio works with compatible content in supported apps. iPhone with TrueDepth camera required to create personalized profile, which will sync across compatible Apple devices. Personalized Spatial Audio is not available when using other devices.
Live Translation is available on compatible Apple devices with the latest operating system software when paired with compatible AirPods with the latest firmware when Apple Intelligence is turned on. Not available in all languages and regions.
Apple Intelligence is available with Siri and device language set to Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, or Vietnamese. Some features may not be available in all regions or languages. Some devices may not be available in all regions. Siri AI is available in beta in iOS 27, macOS 27, and watchOS 27 and requires an Apple Intelligence–enabled device set to a supported language. Available in English to start. Siri AI will not be initially available in the EU on iOS, iPadOS, and watchOS. Certain Apple Intelligence features that rely on server-side models are subject to daily usage limits, including but not limited to Siri AI, Intelligent Photo Editing Tools, Image Playground, and AFM 3 Cloud models in Shortcuts. Daily limits may vary by feature, request complexity, system demand, system policies, and other factors. Expanded access to such features will be available for a fee in the future. Use of these features is subject to the Apple Intelligence Terms and Conditions. Learn more at apple.com/apple-intelligence. Hands-free access to Siri AI works on all AirPods.
Battery life depends on device settings, environment, usage, and many other factors.
Learn more and shop AirPods 5: https://apple.co/4heYN5L

ns2:group.ns2:title: New Apple Watch Series 12: The most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Apple Watch Series 12 has the most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable. Unlock new features like high-frequency heart rate tracking, heart rate variability in daytime vitals, and a readiness score that lets you know when to rest or put yourself to the test. And now every day feels more effortless with Siri Al and Audio Intelligence.
Apple Watch is the ultimate device for a healthy life, with features like sleep score, cycle tracking, and in-depth workout metrics. It’s built to go all day with up to 24-hour battery life, a wide-angle Always-On Retina display, and superdurable Ceramic Shield 2 on aluminum cases.
Learn more about Apple Watch Series 12: https://apple.co/4A1JSTM
Siri AI is rolling out in English. Some Audio Intelligence features coming in beta late 2026. Usage limits may apply.
Apple Intelligence is available with Siri and device language set to Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, or Vietnamese. Some features may not be available in all regions or languages. Some devices may not be available in all regions. Siri AI is available in beta in watchOS 27 and requires an Apple Intelligence–enabled device set to a supported language. Available in English to start. Siri AI will not be initially available in the EU on watchOS. Certain Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features have usage limits. Expanded access to such features will be available for a fee in the future. Use of these features is subject to the Apple Intelligence Terms and Conditions. Learn more at apple.com/apple-intelligence.
Audio Intelligence includes Live Rewind, Siri Recap, Sound Recognition, and faster Shazam and requires Apple Watch Series 12 or Apple Watch Ultra 4. Live Rewind and Siri Recap will be available in beta in late 2026 and require an Apple Intelligence–enabled iPhone 16 or later (excluding iPhone 16e). Will be available in English to start and will not initially be available in the EU. Certain Audio Intelligence features that rely on server-side models are subject to daily usage limits, including but not limited to Live Rewind and Siri Recap. For more information, visit support.apple.com/148354.
Based on data from an Apple-conducted study of heart rate accuracy, during July and August 2026, utilizing commercially available best-selling wearables available as of June 2026. For more information, visit apple.com/HRAccuracy
